CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right upper arm pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female presents with severe right upper arm pain sustained during a volleyball game approximately 18 hours ago. Patient was spiking the ball when an opponent kicked her legs from underneath her, causing her to fall and land on her arm and shoulder. Pain is rated 9/10 in severity. Patient has been taking ibuprofen every 6 hours with minimal relief. No ice has been applied to the injury.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness or tingling in right arm. Physical examination reveals swelling and erythema over right shoulder with tenderness on palpation. Normal pulses. Able to straighten elbow and bend arm when shoulder is not moved. Remainder of physical examination normal.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones
Lumbar fusion 6 years ago

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen (taking every 6 hours)
Pepcid (for gallstones)

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Plays volleyball

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right shoulder with swelling and erythema present. Tenderness over right shoulder. Normal pulses in right arm. Full elbow extension and flexion maintained when shoulder is immobilized. No numbness or tingling. Remainder of body examination normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right arm reveals proximal humerus fracture (fracture of the proximal portion of the humerus).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture, right arm. Plan to treat conservatively with immobilization in long arm cast and sling. Patient to follow up in 2 weeks to assess bone realignment; if inadequate healing, will consider surgical intervention at that time. Prescribed Lortab 5 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed for pain (20 tablets dispensed). Patient instructed on cast and sling care. Discharged to home with follow-up appointment in 2 weeks.
